title: Capture the AST rejection reason at the synthesis_or_ast_failed terminal
acceptance_criteria: In main(), inside the `if not synthesis_success:` terminal block, a lifecycle row is emitted via orch._emit_lifecycle(state_dir, event='ast_validation_failed', task_id=task_id, detail=<summary>) BEFORE the existing orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'synthesis_or_ast_failed') call.

The summary is built from agent_a_violations / agent_b_violations error-severity entries, each prefixed by the originating agent name (e.g. 'agent_a: <rule> L<line> <message>'), so autowork_daemon._get_errors_for_task surfaces the reason to the diagnosing agent.

Because _get_errors_for_task only surfaces a ledger row when the line text contains 'fail' or 'error', the emitted event name 'ast_validation_failed' (which contains 'fail') guarantees the detail is surfaced.
When both violation lists are empty (or contain no error-severity entries), the code degrades gracefully and does not raise; main() still reaches _mark_blocked exactly as today.
The edit is strictly additive: every other code path in main() is byte-identical and harness/orchestrator_worker.py remains importable at module load.

spec.objective: Persist the per-agent AST violation reason as a lifecycle ledger row at the dual-agent reject terminal so the downstream diagnosing agent has a concrete failure cause to act on, closing the first gap in the self-heal loop.
functional_requirements: Build a per-agent AST violation summary string from agent_a_violations and agent_b_violations: include only error-severity Violation entries (v.severity == 'error'), and prefix each entry with the originating agent name (e.g. 'agent_a: <v.rule> L<v.line> <v.message>').

Emit orch._emit_lifecycle(state_dir, event='ast_validation_failed', task_id=task_id, detail=<summary>) immediately BEFORE the existing orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'synthesis_or_ast_failed') call in the `if not synthesis_success:` block (worker reject terminal, around orchestrator_worker.py:312-319).

Degrade gracefully when no error-severity violations exist (empty lists, or only warnings): emit a benign/empty-but-valid detail without raising, and keep main() otherwise byte-identical so module importability and all non-reject paths are unchanged.
spec.interfaces: Uses the existing orch._emit_lifecycle(state_dir, event, task_id, detail) (orchestrator.py:51, **fields signature) and Violation objects exposing .rule/.line/.message/.severity (already in scope at the terminal as agent_a_violations / agent_b_violations). No new public symbols; the new code lives inline in main() at the synthesis_or_ast_failed terminal.
edge_cases: Both violation lists empty -> emit with empty/placeholder detail, still call _mark_blocked.
Violations contain only warning/info severity -> no error entries; summary is empty but emission still succeeds.
A Violation missing optional attributes -> defensive getattr access so summary building never raises.
_emit_lifecycle itself failing must not prevent _mark_blocked from running (do not change blocking behavior).
non_goals: Do NOT weaken or alter the AST AND-gate or any AST rule.
Do NOT change which tasks get blocked or the _mark_blocked reason string ('synthesis_or_ast_failed').
Do NOT modify any other branch of main().
Do NOT set a working_dir front-matter key (self-build).
spec.implementation_notes:
Edits harness/orchestrator_worker.py main(), at the `if not synthesis_success:` reject terminal (currently orchestrator_worker.py:312-319). Place the summary-building + orch._emit_lifecycle(... event='ast_validation_failed' ...) call directly BEFORE the existing orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'synthesis_or_ast_failed') line. Guard the new code in try/except so any exception is swallowed (best-effort telemetry) and the original control flow is preserved. This is an INLINE additive edit to an EXISTING function (no new top-level symbol) -> pipeline-viable as a partial_edit.

[ORACLE CONTRACT - tests/adversarial/test_selfheal_ast_reason_capture.py] The window between `if not synthesis_success:` and `_mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'synthesis_or_ast_failed')` MUST reference the violations (substring 'agent_a_violations' or 'agent_b_violations' or 'violation') AND emit a ledger row (substring '_emit_lifecycle' together with 'detail', OR 'write_jsonl'). The companion round-trip test (test_get_errors_surfaces_ast_violation_detail) is already GREEN and pins the ledger row shape {event:'ast_validation_failed', detail:'...'} that _get_errors_for_task surfaces.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Fabricated agent_a_violations / agent_b_violations lists with mixed severities, an empty-violations case, and a fake state_dir to capture emitted lifecycle rows.

token_budget_ratio.note: Small additive inline change; test weight dominates to lock the RED oracle and byte-identical guarantee.
